newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: RIO TINTO'S ENTERPRISE DEAL FOR HUNTER MINERS
Resouces giant Rio Tinto has released a draft enterprise agreement it has put to the Miners Union as renewed attempts begin to resolve the Hunter Valley mine dispute.
The renewed agreement includes a $20 increase for workers but aims to remove restrictive work practices, such as seniority, and includes an ongoing offer of individual contracts.
Hunter Valley No. 1 mine manager, Allan Davies, says for the moment, the company won't be acting on an industrial commission order directing train drivers to cross the picket line as required.
Mr Davies says he believes the trade-off of extra pay for restrictive work practices is a good deal.
"Well I think in anyone's language this package is a substantially is a very attractive package," Mr Davies said.

"It offers substantial benefits to all employees. People have got to realise that already these guys are earning a substantial amount of money, about twice the national average. And I think to anyone this offer should be very attractive."
VANSTONE SAYS HANSON HATES HER LIFE AND THE WORLD

The Federal Employment Minister, Amanda Vanstone, has made a bitter personal attack on Independent MP Pauline Hanson, accusing her of behaving as though she had an unhappy childhood. Senator Vanstone has devoted almost an entire speech at a Women in Managment luncheon in Melbourne, to criticising the One Nation Party and defending multiculturalism.
She's appealed to Victorians not to protest at Miss Hanson's appearance in Geelong tomorrow, to avoid giving her publicity.
Senator Vanstone says Miss Hanson hates her life and the world, and projects that hate onto others.
"With an ego bigger than Texas, she calls her party Pauline Hanson's One Nation party, and then sets out on a tour to divide," Senator Vanstone said.
"She finds political capital in preying on the people's fears. And remember, this woman offers no solutions, she just keeps frightening people."
Meanwhile, Victoria's Premier Jeff Kennett predicts Pauline Hanson's One Nation Party won't survive the next Federal Election.
Speaking in Geelong, where Miss Hanson will appear tomorrow night, Mr Kennett said her party had been hijacked by extremists of the left and right.
He says One Nation is already harming Australia in Asia, and it could take years to heal the rift.
OPPOSITION UNHAPPY OVER TREASURER'S ROLE IN GOLD SALE
The Federal Opposition has renewed its call for an investigation into Treasurer Peter Costello's role in the Reserve Bank's decision to sell off its gold deposits.
The Prime Minister says he'll make inquiries about the involvement of Western Mining Corporation chief and Reserve Bank Board member, Hugh Morgan, in the decision.
Labor's Resources spokesman, Stephen Smith, says while Mr Howard's at it he should look into the industry and export damage that will result from Mr Costello's handling of the contentious decision.
Mr Smith says it is time for the Prime Minister to make the Treasurer accountable for his role in endorsing and supporting the Reserve Bank's judgement.
HUNDREDS ATTEND DEMOLITION VICTIM'S FUNERAL
In Canberra, up to 1500 people have turned out for the funeral of 12-year-old Katie Bender.
Katie was killed when struck by debris at the demolition of former Royal Canberra Hospital buildings last Sunday.
Police had to direct traffic around St Patricks Church in Braddon as hundreds of cars brought mourners to the service.
Students from Katie's school, St. Clair's, each carried a single yellow daffodil at the Mass.
BABYSITTER IN PROTECTIVE CUSTODY ON MURDER CHARGE
Homicide Squad detectives will spend the next fortnight, preparing their case against Greg Domaszweicz, the man charged with murdering Jaidyn Leskie at Moe in Victoria.
The 28-year old babysitter was placed in protective custody, after being remanded until July 31.
Mr Domaszweicz was taken into court just after 10 o'clock this morning, after spending the night in custody, on a charge of murdering 14-month old Jaidyn Leskie. A body has not been found.
Standing behind a protective glass enclosure, he acknowledged his mother who had travelled to Melbourne for the brief hearing.
Mr Domaszweicz is being separated from other prisoners while in custody, after his barrister John Lee said he feared for his client's safety because of the case's notoriety.
Outside court, Mr Domaszweicz's mother Helen expressed her fears.
"Of course I do. I mean he is innocent. he is not guilty," she said.
Mr Lee says a bail application will be made.
"He maintains his innocence and we'll be applying for bail as soon as possible," Mr Lee said.
